questions.title: What is a piecewise function?
choices: A function defined by a single formula for all x-values
A function defined by different formulas on different intervals of x
A function that is always linear
A function that is always quadratic
questions.explain: A piecewise function uses different rules (formulas) depending on the value of x.

questions.title: Which of the following is a piecewise function?
questions.explain: Only the second option shows different formulas with conditions on x.

questions.title:
Given the function below, which formula is used when x = −2?

<math><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo><lt/></mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></math>
questions.explain: Since −2 < 0, we use the first piece: g(x) = 2x − 1.

questions.title:
Using the same function g(x) from the previous question, what is g(−2)?

<math><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo><lt/></mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></math>

Consider the function:

<math><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo><lt/></mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mi>x</mi></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></math>

Which statement is true about h(x) at x = 0?
choices: h(0) uses the first piece and equals 1
h(0) uses the second piece and equals 0
questions.explain: The condition x ≥ 0 includes x = 0, so h(0) = 0 from the second piece.

questions.title: Which inequality would make the point at x = 3 a closed circle on the graph?
questions.explain: Using ≤ or ≥ includes the endpoint, which is shown with a closed circle.

questions.title:
A piecewise function is defined as:

<math><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable><mtr><mtd><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo><lt/></mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>4</mn></mtd><mtd><mtext>if </mtext><mi>x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow></math>

What is f(1)?
questions.explain: Since 1 ≥ 1, we use the second piece: f(1) = 4.

questions.title: Which description best matches how to evaluate a piecewise function?
choices: Always use the first formula, regardless of x
Use the formula that gives the largest output
Choose the formula based on the condition that x satisfies
Average all formulas and use that value
questions.explain: You must check which interval x is in and then use that specific formula.

questions.title: Why can a piecewise function still be a valid function even if it has multiple formulas?
choices: Because each x-value still has exactly one output
Because each x-value can have many outputs
Because the graph is always continuous
questions.explain: As long as no x-value is assigned more than one y-value, it is still a function.
